monthly_review.summary: You've shifted sharply toward higher-intensity running this month, with significant gains in pace and aerobic training effect—but at the cost of volume and aerobic base work.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 effort jumped from 15% to 43% of total HR time this month — a dramatic shift toward threshold and hard efforts, while Zone 1+2 dropped from 53% to 14%.

goal_tracker.message: You need 43.6 more km across 8 sessions in the remaining 25 days — averaging 5.5 km per session. To match last month’s volume, aim for one 10 km run, three 6 km runs, and four 5 km runs.

insights.title: Efficiency holding steady despite intensity jump
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved marginally from 13.46 to 13.48 m/sec per bpm — impressive given the 10 bpm rise in average HR and 41 sec/km pace improvement, suggesting better neuromuscular coordination under load.

insights.title: Severe aerobic base erosion
insights.body: Time in Zones 1+2 collapsed from 53% (last month) to just 14% (this month), while Zone 4 now dominates at 43% — indicating insufficient recovery and low-intensity volume to sustain long-term aerobic development.

insights.title: Stride length and vertical oscillation improving with pace
insights.body: Stride length increased from 72.2 cm (6.5 km @ 8.93 min/km) to 75.7 cm (10 km @ 8.45 min/km), and vertical oscillation rose only modestly (7.9 → 8.0 cm) — showing efficient power transfer at faster paces.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Your 10 km run on 7/5 had 4.0 Aerobic TE — equivalent to ~75 minutes of Z2 work — yet was preceded by only one easy run (0.9 km) and followed by no rest day; no run in the past 5 had Z1 or Z2 dominance to offset cumulative stress.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤ 138 bpm, pace ~9:00–9:30 min/km) with cadence ≥ 150 spm and ground contact < 320 ms
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Zone 1+2 time (currently only 14%) and restore aerobic resilience after 3 consecutive high-TE sessions

recommendations.action: Insert a full rest day before your next run >6 km — especially before any session targeting Zone 4 or higher
recommendations.reason: Your last 5 runs included zero rest days and accumulated 14.9 km at avg HR ≥ 148 bpm; VO2 max remains stable at 39.0 but recovery metrics (e.g., HRV not provided) are likely compromised

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-second strides (at 3:45–4:00 min/km pace) after your next two easy runs, focusing on landing midfoot and reducing vertical oscillation target to ≤7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased from 7.5 cm (3 km run) to 8.5 cm (0.9 km recovery run), suggesting fatigue-related form breakdown even at low effort — strides reinforce economy under fresh conditions

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish foundational Zone 2 endurance and neuromuscular control to support sustainable intensity gains — prioritizing time-in-zone over pace or distance.
